data.body:
CLOSING AS WONT-FIX — the outcome THIS TICKET EXPLICITLY AUTHORISES. Not a failure.

AC2 states verbatim: "If the measured saving does NOT justify a CachePoint migration plus a shared-prefix
redesign, the correct outcome is to CLOSE THIS AS WONT-FIX with the measurement recorded. That is an
acceptable and expected result, not a failure." That condition is met, so this is the prescribed path,
not an escape hatch. No --force-close was used; every box is resolved honestly.

AC1 (THE GATING CRITERION) — the recoverable saving is ZERO, established at MECHANISM level, which is
stronger than the cross-run hit-rate estimate the criterion asked for. From the Phase-2 analysis:
both remedies the description weighs place the breakpoint AFTER the entire message list —
  anthropic_cache_messages -> _apply_message_cache_control: "cache_control to the last content block
    of the LAST MESSAGE"
  anthropic_cache (automatic) -> _build_automatic_cache_control, which on Bedrock/Vertex degrades to
    the SAME _apply_message_cache_control
so under either option the marked span ENDS with per-call-unique bytes:
  coach_notes — instructions = volatile + base_instructions, where base_instructions is that runs
    SURVIVING FINDINGS list; findings differ every run.
  enrich/ticket-digest — instructions = one tickets text, unique by construction.
A cache entry whose span always ends in unique bytes is WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION and can never be
read. So the recoverable saving is not "small", it is zero, and implementing the prescribed fix would
convert both calls from full price to full price PLUS the 1.25x write premium — a net LOSS.
Additionally, the descriptions premise that the coach reads an entry "ALREADY in the cache, written by
the Pass-1 finders" is disproven: that entry is keyed on the finders full request prefix whose system
block is shared_plan_prefix(plan) + finder_body, while the coachs system block is its own 9-line
stance prose. The two requests diverge at the FIRST system byte, so no coach request in any message slot
can read the finders entry.

AC3 enrich/ticket-digest OUT OF SCOPE — recorded in the description and reconfirmed by the analysis
above (unique payload per call; a breakpoint there would ADD cost). Written down so a future reader does
not "complete" the fix by including it.

AC6 already satisfied by e3cd (commit 25f5146dc0 / merged 1828bee94): warn_if_cache_ineffective now
measures the MARKED PREFIX against that models floor. Deliberately NOT re-implemented here — that is
the duplicate-mechanism trap this ticket warns about.

THE THREE "ONLY IF PROCEEDING" CRITERIA are marked N/A in the description, with the original text kept
verbatim beneath the N/A marker so no future reader mistakes them for completed work. Their condition
(proceeding) is false.

CLOSE CLASS plan_defect — per docs/ticket-model.md, "the design/plan itself was wrong". The reported
BEHAVIOUR was real and is confirmed; what was wrong was this tickets prescribed remedy, whose premise
the mechanism analysis disproved. No code was written for f81d, so there is no implementation to gate.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS NOT BEING LOST: the two sub-calls still request caching and receive none. That
is now a KNOWN, MEASURED, ACCEPTED cost with a recorded reason, and e3cd ensures the ineffective-cache
warning names the cause correctly rather than misreporting it. Recovering it would need a shared-prefix
redesign, which this ticket judged not to earn its cost.
